newsitem.title: USA: Clinton DC plan positive, but hurdles ahead - Moody's.
newsitem.headline: Clinton DC plan positive, but hurdles ahead - Moody's.

text.p: Moody's Investors Service said the Clinton Administration's $3.9 billion plan to revitalize the District of Columbia is a "positive development," but warned that a "strenuous" approval process lies ahead on Capitol Hill.

"Although the Administration's decision to pursue these reforms is a positive development, the proposal must still gain Congressional approval and, in the process, may undergo significant amendment," Moody's said in Friday's edition of Credit Perspectives.
"To the extent that the proposal is able to restore liquidity and establish a better balanced budget, the credit quality of the District's bonds could improve," the report said.
"But, the announcement of the proposal does not alter Moody's outlook for the District," Moody's said.
Moody's currently rates D.C.'s general obligation bonds as Ba - a junk bond rating - with a stable outlook.

The agency said Clinton's plan for D.C., which is expected to be announced next week in the President's fiscal 1998 budget proposal, could yield the city an estimated savings of $770 million over five years.

Moody's noted that while the proposal would address the city's "burdensome" pension deficit and require the U.S. to shoulder a number of major District expenses, it also would wipe out Congress' annual $660 million payment to D.C.

It warned that the plan's broad approach to Medicaid, prison maintenance, court administration, tax collection and transportation means a "strenuous and complex Congressional approval process" lies ahead.
Nevertheless, the plan is a "potential credit positive" for D.C., Moody's said.
